Step 1, #477
Close the holes where harm happens with no prompt

A1: a commit can run any program. A3: /bin/rm and find -delete get past the delete guard. A4: checkout HEAD -- and switch -f discard edits. U5: worktree remove --force gets no decision. A11: autosave pushes untracked files. A8: the installer can empty settings.json. D1: a GitHub comment can approve a stage.
Done when each finding's verify.py case passes, both test suites (verify.py and tools/verify_tools.py) pass, and the audit's proof commands are now refused or ask you first.
unlock
Step 2, #478
Stop the guard refusing routine commands

A5: agent/ branches become the agent's own. A6, H3 and U8: only running a script counts as running it. U6 and H1: single-quoted text and quoted heredocs aren't read as commands, but $(...) in double quotes still is. H2: unstaging is allowed. U7: the first cloud commit gets one refusal that names the full fix, not three.
Done when both test suites (verify.py and tools/verify_tools.py) pass and the verify.py cases for A1 from step 1 still pass.
folder
Step 3, #479
Hand off and free disk without new approvals

U4: folder deletes that git or an install can undo are allowed. U1: "Continue from: <branch>" and "Issues for <feature>: #N" work in your own messages only. U2b: issues from scripts and loops are counted. U2: each approval is pushed at once.
The exact list of deletable folders comes to you on this step's own page before code. Done when a real cloud session shows the handoff and the delete working.
lock
Steps 4 to 6, #480 to #482
Side doors, approvals, tidying

Step 4 closes the ways around the code lock and opens a separate issue for D10, the shell-write gap. Step 5 makes each approval move only what you named. Step 6 fixes the tooling's wrong answers, removes dead code, and measures the hook cost before changing it.
Done when both test suites (verify.py and tools/verify_tools.py) pass after each step.

changes: Six steps, in the order you approved
Each step is one child issue of #476, built and checked before the next starts.
45 findings sit in four audit reports, and none is fixed.
Each fix arrives with its test, one step at a time, with one version bump per step.
The three promises hold in every step: only your messages move a stage, code stays locked before a build plan is approved, and nothing is deleted that can't be brought back.
choices: When should you QA the work?
After each step: you get a QA page per step, and the next step waits for your pass
Six small checks. A problem in step 1's guard patterns is caught before step 2 builds on them.
After steps 1 to 3, then after steps 4 to 6
Two larger checks. Faster, but a problem in step 1 could carry into steps 2 and 3.
My suggestion is A, because steps 1 and 2 change the same guard patterns.
